t: Renaissance humanism began in 14th-century Italy with Petrarch and his followers, who sought to revive the language, literature and moral wisdom of ancient Rome and Greece.
Humanists hunted for lost manuscripts, learned Greek from Byzantine teachers and developed the textual criticism with which Lorenzo Valla exposed the Donation of Constantine as a forgery.
Carried across Europe by printing and by scholars such as Erasmus, its course of grammar, rhetoric, poetry, history and moral philosophy shaped European schooling for four centuries.
dyk: The roman type of most printed books today descends from a handwriting that Poggio Bracciolini and his Florentine circle developed around 1400, copying the Carolingian script of the old manuscripts in which they found the classics.
ev: Petrarch is crowned poet laureate on the Capitoline Hill in Rome
The Byzantine scholar Manuel Chrysoloras begins teaching Greek in Florence
Poggio Bracciolini finds complete texts of Quintilian and Lucretius in monastery libraries
Lorenzo Valla shows that the Donation of Constantine is a forgery
Cosimo de' Medici gives Marsilio Ficino the Greek manuscripts of Plato to translate into Latin
Aldus Manutius begins printing the Greek classics in Venice
Erasmus publishes the Greek New Testament at Basel, with a revised Latin translation and notes
The Jesuits’ Ratio Studiorum makes the humanist course of study the rule in their colleges

f.where: The cities and courts of Italy, above all Florence, Padua, Rome, Naples and Venice; from the late 15th century France, the Low Countries, the German lands, England, Spain, Hungary and Poland
f.period: c. 1340–1600: Italian from Petrarch’s generation to the late 15th century, then European; afterwards the ordinary schooling of educated Europeans
f.figures: Petrarch, Coluccio Salutati, Leonardo Bruni, Lorenzo Valla, Marsilio Ficino, Desiderius Erasmus
f.outcome: The classics of Greece and Rome recovered and printed, the methods of textual criticism founded, and the humanities made the basis of European schooling
